title: Stop abandoned hub work while keeping the live connection
goal: Cancel a non-streaming SignalR invocation and pass its token into server work while keeping the connection usable; requires matched new .NET client/server capabilities.

selectionNotes: Non-streaming invocation; matched new client/server capabilities.
.NET client and ASP.NET Core 11 server together; cancellation is cooperative. A canceled client task does not prove server cleanup.

prerequisites: Both client and server must support non-streaming invocation cancellation. The canonical complete consumers pin SDK 10.0.402 / 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, C# 14 / 15 and client packages 10.0.13 / 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105. Restore matching packs/packages before offline sample use; Playbook itself is offline.
constraints: Non-streaming invocation; matched new client/server capabilities. No .NET 10 target route is declared. Tested mixed pairs retain only local wait cancellation until the connection is stopped.

The server-supplied CancellationToken parameter is not a serialized client argument. Pass the final InvokeAsync token into all cancellable hub work. Cancellation is cooperative, races completion and cannot undo committed effects.
A canceled caller Task does not acknowledge server cleanup. OperationCanceledException escaping the hub is an error completion; SendAsync has no result-waiting invocation to cancel.
The older valid fallback uses a dedicated connection and Context.ConnectionAborted; StopAsync abandons all work on that connection and requires reconnection.

Loopback HTTP observation/control endpoints and the singleton held-work registry are proof instrumentation only. Do not deploy them as a cancellation/authorization service. No browser/Java/Swift client, Azure SignalR Service, MessagePack, database, other transport or platform execution is claimed.
